test_title: PYST 6: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question:
Instructions: Read the Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully. Choose the correct option:
Assertion (A): India launched the South Asian Satellite (SAS) in 2017 for use by SAARC nations.
Reason (R): The SAS was launched from the Sriharikota spaceport, and its terminals were installed in all SAARC countries.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A is true, but R is false**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Assertion (A)** states that **India** launched the **South Asian Satellite (SAS)** in **2017** for use by **SAARC** nations. This statement is **correct**. The satellite, also known as **GSAT-9**, was launched on **May 5, 2017**, as a gift from **India** to its neighboring countries to bolster communication and regional cooperation.

• The **South Asian Satellite** was a brainchild of Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, who proposed the idea during the **18th SAARC Summit** held in **Nepal** in **2014**. The project aimed to provide various communication applications to **South Asian** countries.

• **Reason (R)** states that the **SAS** was launched from the **Sriharikota** spaceport, and its terminals were installed in all **SAARC** countries. This statement is **incorrect**. While the satellite was indeed launched from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** in **Sriharikota** using the **GSLV-F09** rocket, it does not serve all **SAARC** nations.

• **Pakistan**, a key member of **SAARC**, decided to opt out of the project, claiming it had its own space program and technical capabilities. Consequently, the satellite benefits only seven out of the eight **SAARC** members: **India**, **Afghanistan**, **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **Maldives**, **Nepal**, and **Sri Lanka**. Therefore, terminals were not installed in **Pakistan**. ***Hence, statement A is true, but statement R is false.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Technical Specifications:** The **GSAT-9** is a **Geostationary Communication Satellite** developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**. It weighs approximately **2,230 kg** and is equipped with **12 Ku-band transponders**.

• **Mission Life:** The satellite has an intended mission life of more than **12 years**. It is positioned at **48 degrees East** longitude in the geostationary orbit.

• **Applications:** The **South Asian Satellite** provides a wide range of services, including **Tele-education**, **Tele-medicine**, **Disaster Management Support**, **Broadcasting** (DTH), and **VSAT** (Very Small Aperture Terminal) connectivity for banking and government networks.

• **Regional Cooperation:** The project is a significant part of **India**'s **'Neighborhood First'** policy. By providing the satellite services free of charge to participating nations, **India** aimed to strengthen diplomatic ties and aid the socio-economic development of the **South Asian** region.

• **SAARC Overview:** The **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)** was established in **1985**. Its secretariat is located in **Kathmandu, Nepal**. The member states include **Afghanistan**, **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **India**, **Maldives**, **Nepal**, **Pakistan**, and **Sri Lanka**.

**Important Points__**

• **Cost of Project:** The total cost of the **South Asian Satellite** project was approximately **₹235 crore** (around **USD 36 million**), which was entirely funded by the **Government of India**. The participating nations only had to bear the cost of ground station infrastructure and maintenance.

• **Launch Vehicle:** The **GSLV-F09** (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) used for this mission featured the indigenous **Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS)**, marking another milestone for **ISRO**'s heavy-lift capabilities.

• **Ground Terminals:** **India** assisted participating countries like **Bhutan** and **Afghanistan** in setting up the necessary ground stations and terminals to receive and transmit data via the **GSAT-9** satellite.

• **Strategic Importance:** Beyond its functional uses, the satellite serves as a strategic tool for **India** to counter the growing influence of other global powers in the **Indian Ocean** and **South Asian** region by providing essential space-based infrastructure.
